title: IntegrationArchitectureItems
description: Shape of content.items for L1-design-integration-architect. The artifact (integration-architecture.md) is the authoritative, human-readable document; items restates the same facts in queryable structured form so downstream consumers (L1-design-api-spec, L1-design-platform-architect, L1-testing-env-provisioner seeding the stub registry, L1-arch-baseline-generator, gr-L1-architecture-conformance) can read the flow register, contract register and conformance checks without parsing markdown. Meta-points pattern: narrative fields are capped summaries, full prose lives only in the artifact. Two invariants are enforced structurally rather than left to prose. First, a synchronous edge is not expressible without a justification, a timeout, a latency budget and a degraded mode — the four together, because a sync call whose failure behaviour nobody wrote down works perfectly until the callee is down and then fails however the first implementer happened to choose. Second, no invented budget: a latency_budget or timeout that is not PENDING requires a source, and one that is PENDING requires a pending_ref, so a plausible-sounding millisecond figure with nothing behind it fails validation rather than shipping into a register that reads as agreed.

flows.description: INT-4, one entry per edge in the FSA's APP-2 component map — all of them. An edge with no entry here is an ungoverned integration, which is the condition INT-C1 exists to detect. Every entry must also have a matching row in contracts[].

contracts.description: INT-5 initial contract register. One row per contract implied by flows[] — both directions are checked in the self-check, so a flow governed here but absent from flows[], or the reverse, is a defect.

event_taxonomy.description: INT-3.2. Every event classified by KIND, because the kind — not the name — decides ordering, retention and replay policy. May be empty only where the product has no asynchronous edge at all, which given PRIN-03's async default should be visible in the reasoning.

integration_styles.description: INT-2. Includes the explicitly NOT-approved styles with approved:false — recording what is prohibited is half the point of the section, and a prohibition stated nowhere is a prohibition nobody can cite.

trust_boundaries.description: INT-7. One entry per boundary in the FSA's SEC-* model. Exact identity technology is deliberately absent — that belongs to the platform viewpoint.

demand_traceability.description: INT-10. One entry per REQ-INT-* demand, per CON-* constraint whose binding viewpoints include INT, and per principle applied. An unanswered demand belongs in open_questions, not in a hopeful row here.

conformance_checks.description: INT-11. At minimum the three the viewpoint always owes: every cross-context edge has a contract, no cross-context DB grants, every synchronous call is budgeted and has a degraded mode.

pending_decisions.description: INT-12. Every deferred decision with the trigger that reopens it — commonly a latency budget waiting on a TBD boundary condition.

open_questions.description: Gaps this agent must not paper over — a TBD boundary condition carried through, an APP-2 edge that cannot be governed as specified, a flow that would imply a second writer.

Flow.description: One governed cross-context edge. The conditional block below is the agent's central discipline expressed in the schema: choosing 'synchronous' obliges a justification, a latency budget, a timeout and a degraded mode, so a sync edge cannot be registered on convenience alone.

id.description: Sequential, matching the subsection heading in the artifact.

name.description: The flow's name as the artifact's subsection heading states it.

producer_context.description: A bounded context from the FSA's APP-1, named exactly as it appears there.

consumer_context.description: A bounded context from APP-1, or a named external system from the enterprise landscape.

style.description: Asynchronous is the default (PRIN-03). Synchronous requires that the caller needs the result to complete the CURRENT user transaction — 'it is simpler' and 'it is faster to build' are not justifications.

contract_owner.description: The PRODUCING context. A consumer never becomes owner of the contract, nor of the entity behind it.

purpose_summary.description: Capped summary of what the flow achieves. Full prose in the artifact.

sync_justification.description: Required when style is synchronous: why the caller cannot complete its current transaction without the answer. Must name the transaction, not merely assert that the data is needed.

latency_budget.description: The budget taken from the matching nfr-spec.md Performance boundary condition, or the literal 'PENDING'. A TBD boundary condition stays TBD — if nfr-spec.md says 'TBD — needs stakeholder input', this says PENDING, it does not say 200ms.

timeout.description: The timeout, or the literal 'PENDING'. A synchronous dependency with no timeout inherits whatever the HTTP client library defaults to, which is a decision made by a dependency author rather than an architect.

degraded_mode.description: What happens when this integration fails — a real behaviour, required for BOTH styles. It must not be an optimistic assumption about the unknown answer: assuming availability sells goods that do not exist, assuming eligibility lets an unvetted party create regulatory evidence. 'Assume it is fine' is not a degraded mode.

source.description: Required whenever latency_budget is not PENDING: the nfr-spec.md boundary condition, REQ-INT demand or KB standard that grounds it.

pending_ref.description: Required whenever latency_budget or timeout is PENDING — the INT-12 row carrying the trigger.

fsa_edge.description: The APP-2 edge this flow governs, identified so the bidirectional coverage check against the component map is mechanical rather than a judgement.

event_type.description: For an asynchronous flow, the event that carries it — must appear in event_taxonomy[].

contract.description: The contract's name — an API name, or an event type in canonical {context}.{entity}.{event} form.

consumer.description: The consuming context, application or external party. 'TBD' is acceptable for an event with no committed consumer yet — an event nobody consumes is still a published contract.

style.description: Must be one of the approved styles in integration_styles[] with approved:true.

version.description: Explicit version — 'v1' for an API path version, semantic for an event contract. A contract without a version cannot be evolved without breaking someone.

initial_state.description: 'Planned' means the architecture recognises the contract but the producing feature has not necessarily been implemented. At Cycle 0 nearly everything is Planned.

EventKind.description: INT-3.2. Classifying by kind is the domain's most consequential modelling decision: the kind decides ordering, retention and replay, and conflating kinds is how one real-world act becomes two audit records.

event_type.description: Canonical {context}.{entity}.{event}, lowercase, past tense on the event segment. The context segment is a bounded context — never a team, system or product.

kind.description: Per the domain KB's taxonomy. 'evidence' is the one to get right: replaying an evidence event does not re-deliver a fact, it asserts the fact a second time.

owner_context.description: The producing context, which owns the event's business meaning.

ordering.description: The ordering guarantee this kind requires — e.g. 'per aggregate, strict' for evidence, 'best-effort; late and out-of-order arrivals are normal' for movement.

replay_policy.description: Whether and how the event may be replayed. For evidence events the policy is usually 'never' — and that must be stated, not left implied by the kind.

deduplication_key.description: What the consumer deduplicates on. For trade and evidence events this derives from the business act (party + subject + business timestamp), never from a message id a producer might regenerate on retry.

reasoning.description: Why this kind, and what follows from it. Not a restatement of what the event announces.

use_summary.description: Capped summary of when this style applies — or, for approved:false, why it is prohibited.

example_edge.description: A real edge from this product using this style. Required when approved is true — a permitted style with no example is a style nobody knows how to apply.

approved.description: false records a deliberately prohibited style (database integration, shared mutable tables, unmanaged point-to-point file exchange). Recording the prohibition is half the section's value.

boundary.description: Where the boundary sits, named against the FSA's SEC-* model.

identity_source.description: Where caller identity originates for traffic crossing here, at capability level. External parties are never on the employee identity provider (kb-L1-enterprise-security ES1). The exact identity PRODUCT belongs to the platform viewpoint and must not appear.

controls_summary.description: Capped summary of what happens at the boundary: identity established, authorization applied, correlation preserved.

demand_id.description: Id exactly as the FSA or the principle catalogue states it, never renumbered.

satisfied_by.description: The INT section that answers it.

satisfaction_summary.description: Capped summary of HOW it is satisfied — the decision, not a restatement of the demand.

check.description: A machine-evaluable expression — e.g. 'count(cross_context_database_grants) == 0'. Prose here makes the check unevaluable, which makes it a slogan.

trigger.description: The condition that reopens this decision, stated as a condition and not a date. PRIN-01-C1 checks exactly this.

question.description: The decision someone has to make, phrased so it can be answered.

origin.description: 'ownership_conflict' — a flow that would imply a second writer for an entity DAT-1 owns elsewhere; raised against the FSA's boundaries, never registered as a flow. 'domain_pattern_conflict' — the domain KB's pattern and a REQ-INT demand disagree; raised rather than silently resolved in either direction.

doc_location.description: The INT section where this question is visible in the artifact. A question recorded only in items is invisible to everyone who reads the document.
